items.title: Iran says it's ready for US ground invasion, rejects ceasefire

featured_image.name: Iran foreign minister says U.S. invasion disaster for them

items.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on Thursday that Iran is prepared to confront American forces if the United States launches a ground invasion, warning it would be "a big disaster for them." Speaking in an exclusive interview with NBC News from Tehran, Araghchi struck a defiant tone, saying Iran has no interest in negotiations or a ceasefire as US and Israeli strikes on the country enter their second week.[1][2]

items.title: Trump backs Kurdish offensive against Iran, says goal is 'to win'

featured_image.name: Trump spoke with Kurdish leaders on Iran at Netanyahu's ...

items.description:
President Donald Trump on Thursday voiced support for Kurdish forces launching an offensive into Iran, telling Reuters in an interview, "I think it's wonderful that they want to do that, I'd be all for it." When asked whether the United States would provide or had offered air cover, Trump said, "I can't tell you that," but added that the objective for the Kurds would be "to win."[1]

The remarks came as The Washington Post reported that Trump had offered "extensive U.S. aircover" and other backing to anti-regime Iranian Kurdish groups during calls with Kurdish minority leaders in Iran and Iraq earlier this week.[2]

items.title: Trump calls Israeli President Herzog a 'disgrace,' demands Netanyahu pardon
items.description:
President Donald Trump on Thursday escalated his campaign to secure a pardon for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, telling Channel 12 in a phone interview that President Isaac Herzog should grant clemency "today" so the embattled leader can focus on the ongoing war with Iran.[1][2]

"I want him to concentrate on the war, not on the f---ing court case," Trump told Axios separately on Thursday, adding that "the only pressure I want on Bibi is to combat Iran".[3]

items.title: Two marsupials believed extinct for 6,000 years found alive in Papua

featured_image.name: Two marsupials believed extinct for 6000 years found alive

items.description: A ring-tailed glider and a pygmy long-fingered possum, both previously known to science only from fossils found in Australia, have been discovered alive in the tropical forests of Papua, Indonesia. The rediscovery, led by Tim Flannery of the Australian Museum in Sydney and aided by local Indigenous communities, represents what researchers are calling an unprecedented find in mammalian biology.

items.title: Iranian missile strike sparks fire at Bahrain's BAPCO refinery

featured_image.name: Moment of Iran strike on US military base in Bahrain - Al Jazeera

items.description:
An Iranian ballistic missile struck a unit of Bahrain's BAPCO Energies refinery on Thursday, sparking a fire that was quickly contained, with no injuries reported and refinery operations continuing, according to Bahrain's National Communication Centre.[1][2]

The strike targeted the Sitra refinery complex, Bahrain's sole and primary oil processing facility, which has a refining capacity of roughly 380,000 to 405,000 barrels per day. Videos circulating on social media showed flames and smoke rising from the Ma'ameer industrial area where the refinery is located. Bahrain's government said an assessment of the damage was underway.[3][4][5][1]

items.title: Saudi Arabia triples Red Sea oil exports as Hormuz blockade fills Gulf storage

featured_image.name: Aramco Explores Oil Exports From Red Sea to Avoid Hormuz ...

items.description:
Saudi Arabia is racing to divert millions of barrels of crude oil to its Red Sea port of Yanbu as the war between the United States, Israel, and Iran chokes off the Strait of Hormuz, the world's most critical oil shipping lane.

Five supertankers have already loaded at Yanbu in the first days of March, tripling the port's average February export volume, according to tanker-tracking data compiled by Bloomberg. Aramco, the world's largest oil exporter, has informed buyers of its Arab Light crude that they must now load cargoes at the western port, according to Reuters.[1][2][3]

items.title: Scientists grow chickpeas in simulated moon dirt

featured_image.name: Scientists successfully harvest chickpeas from 'moon dirt'

items.description: As NASA prepares to return astronauts to the moon with the Artemis program, researchers at the University of Texas at Austin and Texas A&M University have answered a pressing question about what future lunar explorers might eat. The answer, according to a study published this week in the journal Scientific Reports, could be chickpeas.

items.title: Trump says he must help pick Iran's next leader

featured_image.name: Trump says Iran war projected to last 4 to 5 weeks, could go ‘far longer’

items.description:
President Donald Trump told Axios on Thursday that he needs to be directly involved in selecting Iran's next supreme leader, an extraordinary assertion of American influence over the internal succession of a sovereign nation now in the throes of a wartime leadership crisis.

"Khamenei's son is unacceptable to me. We want someone that will bring harmony and peace to Iran," Trump said in the interview, referring to Mojtaba Khamenei, son of the late Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. "I have to be involved in the appointment, like with Delcy in Venezuela," he added, drawing a direct parallel to the U.S.-backed removal of Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro earlier this year.[1][2]

Axios co-founder Jim VandeHei, who shared the exclusive, described Trump's stance as "Regime Change, Part 2," noting the president "will personally help pick the next leader of Iran" and called Khamenei's son "a weak, unacceptable option".[3]

items.description: The escalating conflict in the Middle East is delivering an unexpected financial lifeline to Moscow, as disruptions to oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz have pushed global crude prices sharply higher — boosting revenues for an energy-dependent economy that entered 2026 in dire fiscal straits.
